sources.title: 10 things you should know about the eVisa
sources.publisher: Government of the Republic of Moldova eVisa portal
sources.officialityEvidence: The Moldova MFA's visa-regime page links this eVisa.gov.md site as the Government's e-visa portal. On 21 August 2026, the portal's server omitted a trusted TLS issuer chain even though its leaf certificate covered both hostnames and remained valid; users must not bypass certificate warnings.
sources.supportingExcerpt: An eVisa is an authorization to enter Moldova issued in PDF format.

policies.title: Moldovan ordinary passport: citizen entry
policies.summary: A person travelling on a Moldovan ordinary passport is classified as a Moldovan citizen, not under the foreign-visitor visa regime.
conditions: The Border Police states that Moldovan citizens have the right to leave and enter Moldova on a passport issued by the competent authorities.
This citizenship classification does not establish foreign-passport, dual-national document choice, residence, work, transit, or final border-control treatment.

policies.title: Named foreign ordinary passports: visa-free visitor baseline
policies.summary: Moldova's current MFA schedule expressly exempts these foreign nationalities from the visa requirement; Hong Kong and Macao are included only on the stated SAR-passport basis and Qatar is listed under bilateral accords.
conditions: This is the ordinary foreign-passport visitor baseline inferred from the MFA's nationality exemption list. Hong Kong and Macao are expressly limited to holders of their respective SAR passports; Qatar is a separate bilateral-accord exemption.
The cited live schedule does not provide a single duration for this full group, so this candidate does not normalize a length of stay from older embassy pages or country-specific agreements.
It does not establish work, residence, airport transit, refugee, emergency, diplomatic, service, special, identity-card, or other travel-document treatment.

Foreign entrants must hold an accepted valid travel document, meet purpose/means and onward-travel requirements where applicable, and remain subject to refusal, security, public-health, document-validity and final-admission checks.

policies.title: Named foreign ordinary passports: electronic visitor visa available before travel
policies.summary: The MFA's current schedule requires these nationalities to hold a visa, and Moldova's official eVisa portal says all foreigners may request a PDF eVisa for eligible transit or short-stay purposes. This is a genuine electronic-issuance route, not merely online filing.
conditions: The official portal says the eVisa is issued in PDF form and has the same entry right as a sticker visa. Only transit B and short-stay C visas can be obtained online; airport-transit A and long-stay D require a diplomatic mission or consular office.

The portal says all foreigners may request eVisa for listed purposes including business, tourism, visits, mission, sports, transport, culture, humanitarian and scientific activities. It does not establish work, study/residence, airport-transit, diplomatic, service, emergency, refugee or other special-document access.

On 21 August 2026, normal TLS verification of the official portal failed because its server omitted a trusted issuer chain. This transport defect is an operational warning, not evidence that electronic issuance ended; users must not bypass browser certificate warnings.

MFA's required-visa list makes a separate invitation procedure applicable to named nationalities and retains exceptions from that procedure. Its [2] nationalities can instead travel while holding a valid non-transit EU/Schengen, UK, US or Canadian visa or residence permit; that document-conditioned alternative does not change this nationality baseline.

For Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Turkmenistan and Vietnam, MFA footnote [1] preserves treaty-based diplomatic, service and special-passport exceptions; those documents are outside this ordinary-passport policy.
Foreign entrants remain subject to accepted-document, purpose, means, onward-travel, refusal, security, public-health, passport-validity and final border-admission requirements.

application.label: Moldova Government eVisa portal
application.processingTime: The official eVisa guidance says a request is processed in up to 10 days.
steps: Use the Government eVisa portal to select an eligible transit B or short-stay C purpose and complete the application.
Supply the portal's required passport, purpose and any invitation-related materials, then pay the applicable fee.
Receive the PDF eVisa before travel and carry the relevant documents for Border Police admission checks.
